newsitem.title: POLAND: Bank Handlowy to advise Polish telecom on its sale.
newsitem.headline: Bank Handlowy to advise Polish telecom on its sale.

text.p: Poland's biggest commercial Bank Handlowy SA signed an agreement with state-owned telecommunications monopoly TPSA to advise on its privatisation, TPSA's spokesman said on Thursday.
Krzysztof Bartnicki said the deal also envisaged Handlowy providing a wide range of banking services for TPSA, including investment credit and guarantees of up to $250 million.
"Bank Handlowy SA, on the basis of an agreement signed with Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), will advise it in the process of privatisation," PAP news agency quoted Bartnicki as saying.
Last month the government's economic committee recommended to the cabinet that the sale of TPSA should start in 1998 with a public offer to domestic and foreign investors.
The second stage of the privatisation could include an offer for a strategic investor.
The net profit of TPSA fell in 1996 to 850 million zlotys from 933 million in 1995.
